features.summary: WebRender, Firefox’s GPU compositor, now does more of its clipping, batching, and visibility work directly in device space, reducing repeated coordinate conversions and limiting image sampling to pixels that are actually visible. Borders, text, glyphs, and line decorations are rasterized using the target surface’s scale, improving sharpness across zoom levels, high-DPI displays, perspective transforms, and nested surfaces; backdrop-filter and underlay/overlay handling also received important correctness fixes. Cleanup of unused paths and new Wrench reftests make the compositor simpler to maintain and better covered by tests.

features.summary: Compositing and layers gained several reliability and security improvements, including stricter validation of scroll data and texture descriptors, limiting capture requests to the root WebRender bridge, and making dummy textures readable under memory pressure. Texture and buffer recycling was expanded for WebGL and WebGPU on Linux and Android, while synchronization fences and remote image color metadata improve graphics stability and color accuracy. The work also updates overscroll-behavior to support the standard “chain” value, brings timeline behavior closer to specification, and fixes HDR video rendering and platform-specific issues on Windows and Wayland.

Hardware video-encoding checks were added to graphics sanity testing, DRM configuration now responds when preferences change, and font state is better protected for safe concurrent use.

CanvasRenderingContext2D now has faster drawing paths for lines and circles, and circle fill events are generated only for valid positive radii, improving both efficiency and correctness.

features.summary: Hardware Windows Media Foundation (WMF) encoders are now created and enumerated in the GPU process, keeping media work better isolated from the browser process. Media IPC also gained a structured RemoteType representation, making process-type information clearer and less error-prone when passed between components.

features.summary: WebGPU updated its wgpu graphics library revision, bringing newer implementation fixes and behavior from the upstream project. DXGI textures are now recycled between WebGL and WebGPU, reducing repeated allocation and release overhead on Windows.

features.summary: WebRender bindings avoid creating and releasing a texture for every frame during direct scanout, improving video presentation efficiency by locking buffers without a GL context. ShaderBlt now handles HDR BT.2100 PQ full-range NV12 video, preserving the intended brightness and color when HDR video is displayed.

features.summary: Graphics configuration received a small cleanup of WebRender preference usage, removing outdated or unnecessary preference handling. _This is maintenance work with no intended visible behavior change._

patches.subject: Part 4. Update Glean/telemetry documentation for new gfx sanity test values.

features.summary: The graphics sanity tests now have updated Glean telemetry documentation describing their new values. This makes the collected graphics-health data easier to interpret and maintain, _without changing what users see_.

features.label: Graphics core internals

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2069594. Give nsRect the default copy constructor so the compiler knows it is trivially copyable.

features.summary: nsRect now has a standard copy constructor, allowing the compiler to recognize that the rectangle type can be copied efficiently as a simple, trivially copyable value. This is an internal optimization and correctness improvement with no visible change.

features.label: Image decoding

patches.author: serge-sans-paille

features.summary: Image-decoding code was simplified by removing an unnecessary inequality comparison specification. The change reduces internal complexity while preserving the same decoding behavior.

They also handle HDR BT.2100 PQ full-range NV12 video—a high-dynamic-range format used by some hardware pipelines—and detect graphics-device resets during screenshots, improving HDR playback and recovery reliability.

features.label: Fontations Glue

patches.author: Jonathan Kew
patches.subject: Have skrifa_font_get_metrics() return zero rather than NaN for unavailable metrics.

patches.author: Jonathan Kew
patches.subject: Use gecko's gfxFontVariation type in fontations_glue, rather than defining a new type for the interface.

patches.author: Emily McDonough
patches.subject: Add basic cbindgen.toml for gfx/fontations_glue

features.summary: Firefox is consolidating its Rust-based font library, Fontations, by standardizing how missing font metrics are reported, eliminating duplicate type definitions, and improving the build tooling that keeps the Rust code coordinated with Firefox's C++ engine.

features.label: Rust

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2065753. Decode JXL images on a dedicated thread pool.

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2064595. Pass None for the new parallel-runner argument at the jxl-rs flush_pixels and process call sites.

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2064595. Upgrade jxl-rs to 0.6.0.

features.summary: JPEG XL decoding in Rust was upgraded to jxl-rs 0.6.0 and moved onto a dedicated thread pool, allowing parallel image work without tying up more general browser threads. The related API updates pass the new parallel-runner setting explicitly, supporting faster and more responsive JPEG XL decoding.

patches.author: Andy Leiserson
patches.subject: WebGPU tests not running on MacOS in release branch CI

features.summary: WebGPU testing infrastructure was updated with test suite improvements and the latest WebGPU Conformance Test Suite (CTS) to ensure Firefox's WebGPU implementation—the graphics API for compute-intensive tasks on the GPU—stays compliant with the latest spec.

features.label: Canvas tests

patches.author: Nicholas Rishel
patches.subject: Validate draw fetch limits for matrix attribute columns.

patches.author: Exploding-Joysticks
patches.subject: Remove the media.rvfc.enable pref

features.summary: Canvas testing now checks that matrix attribute columns stay within WebGL draw-fetch limits, catching invalid GPU input earlier. An obsolete media.rvfc.enable preference was removed as the related behavior is no longer controlled by that setting.

features.label: Graphics configuration

patches.author: Emilio Cobos Álvarez
patches.subject: Cleanup some webrender pref usage.

patches.author: stransky
patches.subject: Bug 2045970 [Linux] Enable Vulkan decode on Nightly and recent NVIDIA devices

features.summary: Firefox’s graphics configuration was simplified by removing outdated WebRender preference usage. On Linux Nightly, Vulkan image decoding is now enabled for recent NVIDIA devices, which can improve decoding performance by using the graphics hardware more directly.

features.label: Virtual & augmented reality

patches.author: Maurice Dauer
patches.subject: Keep the window name as UTF-16,

patches.author: Nika Layzell
patches.subject: Part 1: Unify IPDL actor devirutalization logic, and require types to be fully qualified,

features.summary: Virtual and augmented reality code now preserves window names as UTF-16 and uses a unified, stricter approach for devirtualizing IPDL actors with fully qualified types. These are compatibility and maintainability improvements _with no major visible change expected_.

features.label: WebGPU backend (wgpu)

patches.author: Erich Gubler
patches.subject: build(webgpu): update wgpu to f7ebc076619e8e6f55def9a13199c1ccc02cc4b4

features.summary: The WebGPU backend (wgpu) was bumped to a newer upstream commit and received related bug fixes. Upgrading wgpu brings upstream compatibility and stability fixes into Firefox’s WebGPU implementation, which can improve driver interactions and performance; these are backend-level improvements rather than new web-facing features.

features.label: Docs

patches.author: canalun
patches.subject: Add a diagram of the architecture around APZCTreeManager.

features.summary: Documentation now includes a diagram of the APZCTreeManager architecture, making it easier to understand how async pan/zoom (touch and scroll handling) is structured and how different pieces interact.

features.label: Graphics core

patches.author: Andrew Osmond
patches.subject: Part 4. Update Glean/telemetry documentation for new gfx sanity test values.

features.summary: The graphics sanity tests now have updated Glean telemetry documentation describing their new values. This makes the collected graphics-health data easier to interpret and maintain, _without changing what users see_.

features.label: Graphics core internals

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2069594. Give nsRect the default copy constructor so the compiler knows it is trivially copyable.

features.summary: nsRect now has a standard copy constructor, allowing the compiler to recognize that the rectangle type can be copied efficiently as a simple, trivially copyable value. This is an internal optimization and correctness improvement with no visible change.

features.label: Graphics tests

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Replace mention of XP_ANDROID define by ANDROID

features.summary: Graphics tests were modernized by replacing the old XP_ANDROID build define with ANDROID, keeping test configuration aligned with current platform macros and reducing platform‑specific confusion.

features.label: Tests (gtest)

patches.author: Nicholas Rishel
patches.subject: Add UploadInitMemTracker to manage zeroing memory for partial texture uploads and marking uninitialized memory as initialized.

features.summary: Graphics test infrastructure got better memory tracking for partial texture uploads. This helps catch uninitialized GPU memory and upload mistakes earlier, improving confidence that the rendering pipeline stays correct even before user-facing features change.
